variables.meaning: heat, the spontaneous transfer of energy due to a temperature difference
the temperature of the soft drink before it is placed in contact with the ice
the temperature of the ice before it is placed in contact with the soft drink
the common temperature the soft drink and the ice reach at thermal equilibrium
the work that produces the same effects as a heat transfer, in Joule's experiment the work done by the falling weights
the heat transferred to change the temperature of a body
the mass of the substance whose temperature changes
the specific heat, the heat needed to change the temperature of 1.00 kg of the substance by 1.00 °C; it depends on the material and its phase
the specific heat of a gas at constant volume
the specific heat of a gas at constant pressure
the change in temperature of the body, the same in kelvin and in degrees Celsius
the final temperature, after the heat transfer or at thermal equilibrium
the initial temperature, before the heat transfer
the heat lost by the hotter body in a calorimetry problem, a negative quantity
the heat gained by the colder body in a calorimetry problem, a positive quantity
the heat required to change the phase of a sample, or released when it changes back
the mass of the sample that changes phase
the latent heat of fusion, the heat per kilogram that melts a substance at its melting point and is released when it freezes
the latent heat of vaporization, the heat per kilogram that vaporizes a substance at its boiling point and is released when it condenses
the heat of sublimation, the heat per kilogram that changes a substance from the solid phase directly to the vapor phase
the latent heat coefficient, standing for whichever of the heats of fusion, vaporization or sublimation the phase change calls for
the final temperature once the ice has melted and the water and the soda have reached thermal equilibrium
the specific heat of the liquid that warms after the phase change, water's in the worked example
the heat conducted through the slab in the time t
the time over which the heat is conducted
the thermal conductivity of the material, the property of its ability to conduct heat
the surface area of the slab through which heat is conducted
the thickness of the slab, the distance the heat is conducted through
the temperature of the hotter face of the slab
the temperature of the colder face of the slab
the temperature of the hotter body, in the temperature difference that drives the heat flux
the temperature of the colder body, in the temperature difference that drives the heat flux
the temperature difference between the hot body and the cold body, which the heat flux depends on
the R factor of an insulator, the ratio of its thickness to its conductivity; the larger it is, the better the insulation
the heat of fusion of the ice the conducted heat melts in the ice-box example
the heat carried by the mass of fluid that convection moves
the time in which the fluid is moved or replaced
the mass of fluid that convection moves, or the mass of water that evaporates
the specific heat of the fluid, for air the specific heat at constant pressure
the temperature change the moved fluid undergoes
the density of the fluid, from which its mass follows for a given volume
the volume of fluid moved, the volume of the house in the worked example
the heat of vaporization of the sweat that evaporates from the skin, 2430 kJ/kg at body temperature
the heat radiated by an object in the time t
the net heat transferred to an object by radiation, its absorption minus its emission
the time over which the radiation is emitted or absorbed
the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ J/(s·m²·K⁴)
the emissivity of the object, a measure of how well it radiates, 1 for a black body and 0 for a perfect reflector
the surface area of the radiating object
the absolute temperature of the radiating object, in kelvin
the absolute temperature of the object
the uniform absolute temperature of the object's surroundings
